answer: Rate-limited registration stops sybil farms at the door: each new agent identity must pass a slow, human-reviewed onboarding queue, so creating ten thousand fake accounts takes months instead of minutes. A trust bridge links each verified identity to a single vertex in the reputation graph, and every newcomer starts as a cold ember with no voting or payout rights until it has done real, attested work over several epochs. An attacker pays in time and visible effort per identity, which makes mass forgery uneconomic.
